title: Arakhin 29
description: Chapter 8, HaMakdish Sadehu, closes with priests’ dedications, Rav’s reversed mishna, the man in Pumbedita who dedicated his property, what applies only when the Jubilee is observed, and Rabbi Yishmael’s two verses on the firstborn, and chapter 9, HaMokher Sadehu, opens: a sold field may not be redeemed for two years, and Rav and Shmuel on a field sold in the Jubilee Year itself.
topics: 🏛️ Priests’ dedications: sacred in the owner’s house, non-sacred once given to the priest
🔄 Rav rules like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, in a mishna taught the other way around
💰 Pumbedita: four dinars thrown into the river, or Ulla’s “all of it to the priests”
📯 Hebrew slave, ancestral field, walled houses, ger toshav: only when the Jubilee is observed
🐑 “You shall consecrate” and “shall not consecrate”: Rabbi Yishmael on the firstborn
📖 Hadran: chapter 8, HaMakdish Sadehu, ends and chapter 9, HaMokher Sadehu, begins
🌾 A sold field: two years of crops before redemption, and three crops in two years
⚖️ Sold in the Jubilee Year itself: Rav, Shmuel, and the two rulings Rav Anan heard

a1.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חֶרְמֵי כֹהֲנִים אֵין לָהֶן פִּדְיוֹן וְנִותָּנִין לַכֹּהֵן. חֲרָמִים כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁהֵן בְּבֵית בְּעָלִים הֲרֵי הֵן כְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ לְכׇל דִּבְרֵיהֶן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים הוּא לַה׳״. נְתָנָן לְכֹהֵן — הֲרֵי הֵן לְכׇל דִּבְרֵיהֶן כְּחוּלִּין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְךָ יִהְיֶה״.

a2.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא אוֹמֵר: סְתַם חֲרָמִים לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת כּוּ׳. בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבָּנַן כִּדְקָא מְפָרְשִׁי טַעְמַיְיהוּ וְטַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא, אֶלָּא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא הַאי ״כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ?

a3.he: מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא: ״כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר? מִנַּיִן לְכֹהֵן שֶׁהִקְדִּישׁ שְׂדֵה חֶרְמוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר: הוֹאִיל וְיוֹצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים, וַהֲרֵי הִיא תַּחַת יָדִי — תְּהֵא שֶׁלִּי?

a4.he: וְדִין הוּא: בְּשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים אֲנִי זוֹכֶה, בְּשֶׁל עַצְמִי לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״.

a5.he: וְכִי מָה לָמַדְנוּ מִשְּׂדֵה חֵרֶם מֵעַתָּה? הֲרֵי זֶה בָּא לְלַמֵּד וְנִמְצָא לָמֵד: מַקִּישׁ שְׂדֵה חֶרְמוֹ לִשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל.

a6.he: מָה שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, יוֹצְאָה מִתַּחַת יָדוֹ, וּמִתְחַלֶּקֶת לַכֹּהֲנִים, אַף שָׂדֶה חֶרְמוֹ, יוֹצְאָה מִתַּחַת יָדוֹ, וּמִתְחַלֶּקֶת לְאֶחָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים.

a7.he: וְאִידָּךְ? מֵ״חֵרֶם״ ״הַחֵרֶם״. וְאִידַּךְ, ״חֵרֶם״ ״הַחֵרֶם״ לָא מַשְׁמַע לֵיהּ.

a8.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא, דְּחָל עַל קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים וְעַל קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, מְנָא לֵיהּ? סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.

a9.he: אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא, וְרַב שָׁבֵיק רַבָּנַן וְעָבֵיד כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא? בָּרַיְיתָא אִיפְּכָא תַּנְיָא, שָׁבֵיק מַתְנִיתִין וְעָבֵיד כְּבָרַיְיתָא? רַב מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי אִיפְּכָא תָּנֵי.

a10.he: מַאי חֲזֵית דְּאָפְכַתְּ מַתְנִיתִין מִקַּמֵּי בָּרַיְיתָא? נֵפֵיךְ בָּרַיְיתָא מִקַּמֵּי מַתְנִיתִין! רַב גְּמָרֵיהּ גְּמִיר. אִי הָכִי, כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא? כְּרַבָּנַן מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ! הָכִי קָאָמַר: לְמַאי דְּאָפְכִיתוּ וְתָנֵיתוּ, הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא.

a11.he: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאַחְרְמִינְהוּ לְנִכְסֵיהּ בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא, אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שְׁקוֹל אַרְבְּעָה זוּזֵי וְאַחֵיל עֲלַיְיהוּ, וּשְׁדִינְהוּ בְּנַהֲרָא, וְלִישְׁתְּרוֹ לָךְ. אַלְמָא קָסָבַר: סְתַם חֲרָמִים לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת.

a12.he: כְּמַאן? כִּשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר: הֶקְדֵּשׁ שָׁוֶה מָנֶה שֶׁחִילְּלוֹ עַל שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה מְחוּלָּל. אֵימַר דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל שֶׁחִילְּלוֹ, לְכַתְּחִלָּה מִי אָמַר?

a13.he: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים, דְּאִיכָּא פְּסֵידָא, אֲבָל בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה אֲפִילּוּ לְכַתְּחִלָּה. אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ פְּרוּטָה נָמֵי? פַּרְסוֹמֵי מִלְּתָא.

a14.he: אָמַר עוּלָּא: אִי הֲוַאי הָתָם, הֲוָה יָהֵיבְנָא כּוּלְּהוּ לְכֹהֲנִים. אַלְמָא קָסָבַר עוּלָּא: סְתַם חֲרָמִים לַכֹּהֲנִים.

a15.he: מֵיתִיבִי: אֵין עֶבֶד עִבְרִי נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַיּוֹבֵל נוֹהֵג, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״עַד שְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל יַעֲבֹד עִמָּךְ״.

a16.he: וְאֵין שְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם נוֹהֶגֶת אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַיּוֹבֵל נוֹהֵג, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְיָצָא בַּיּוֹבֵל וְשָׁב לַאֲחֻזָּתוֹ״. אֵין בָּתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה נוֹהֲגִין אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַיּוֹבֵל נוֹהֵג, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לֹא יֵצֵא בַּיּוֹבֵל״.

a17.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר: אֵין שְׂדֵה חֲרָמִין נוֹהֲגִין אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַיּוֹבֵל נוֹהֵג, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיּוֹבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳ כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם״. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אֵין גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַיּוֹבֵל נוֹהֵג.

a18.he: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי: מַאי טַעְמָא? אַתְיָא ״טוֹב״ ״טוֹב״, כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״כִּי טוֹב לוֹ עִמָּךְ״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״בַּטּוֹב לוֹ לֹא תּוֹנֶנּוּ״!

a19.he: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בִּמְקַרְקְעֵי, הָא בְּמִטַּלְטְלֵי. וְהָא מַעֲשֶׂה דְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא בִּמְקַרְקְעֵי נָמֵי הֲוָה! מְקַרְקְעֵי דְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ כְּמִטַּלְטְלֵי דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל דָּמֵי.

a20.he: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר ״תַּקְדִּישׁ״, וְכָתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר ״לֹא יַקְדִּישׁ״. אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר ״תַּקְדִּישׁ״ — שֶׁהֲרֵי כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר ״לֹא יַקְדִּישׁ״, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר ״לֹא יַקְדִּישׁ״ — שֶׁהֲרֵי כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר ״תַּקְדִּישׁ״.

a21.he: הָא כֵּיצַד? מַקְדִּישׁוֹ אַתָּה הֶקְדֵּשׁ עִלּוּי, וְאִי אַתָּה מַקְדִּישׁוֹ הֶקְדֵּשׁ מִזְבֵּחַ.

a22.he: גּמ׳, וְרַבָּנַן: ״אַל תַּקְדִּישׁ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְלָאו, ״תַּקְדִּישׁ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא: מִנַּיִן לְנוֹלַד בְּכוֹר בְּעֶדְרוֹ שֶׁמִּצְוָה לְהַקְדִּישׁוֹ? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הַזָּכָר תַּקְדִּישׁ״.

a23.he: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, אִי לָא מַקְדֵּישׁ לֵיהּ, לָא קָדֵישׁ? קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ מֵרֶחֶם הוּא, וְכֵיוָן דְּכִי לָא מַקְדֵּישׁ לֵיהּ קָדוֹשׁ, לָא צְרִיךְ לְאַקְדּוֹשֵׁיהּ.

b1.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת שָׂדֵהוּ בִּשְׁעַת הַיּוֹבֵל — אֵינוֹ מוּתָּר לִגְאוֹל פָּחוֹת מִשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בְּמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי תְבוּאֹת יִמְכׇּר לָךְ״.

b2.he: הָיְתָה שְׁנַת שִׁדָּפוֹן וְיֵרָקוֹן, אוֹ שְׁנַת שְׁבִיעִית — אֵינָו עוֹלָה מִן הַמִּנְיָן. נָרָהּ אוֹ הוֹבִירָהּ — עוֹלָה לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מְכָרָהּ לוֹ לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְהִיא מְלֵיאָה פֵּירוֹת — הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹכֵל מִמֶּנָּה שָׁלֹשׁ תְּבוּאוֹת בִּשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים.

b3.he: גְּמָ׳ הַמּוֹכֵר שָׂדֵהוּ בִּשְׁעַת הַיּוֹבֵל וְכוּ׳. ״אֵינוֹ גּוֹאֵל״ לָא קָתָנֵי, אֶלָּא ״אֵינוֹ מוּתָּר לִגְאוֹל״, אַלְמָא קָסָבַר: אִיסּוּרָא נָמֵי אִיכָּא, דַּאֲפִילּוּ קַרְקוֹשֵׁי זוּזֵי נָמֵי אָסוּר.

b4.he: וְלָא מִיבַּעְיָא מוֹכֵר, דְּקָאֵי בַּעֲשֵׂה, דִּכְתִיב: ״בְּמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי תְבוּאֹת יִמְכׇּר לָךְ״, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ לוֹקֵחַ נָמֵי קָאֵי בַּעֲשֵׂה, דְּבָעֵינַן ״שָׁנִים תִּקְנֶה״, וְלֵיכָּא.

b5.he: אִיתְּמַר: הַמּוֹכֵר שָׂדֵהוּ בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל עַצְמָהּ, רַב אָמַר: מְכוּרָה וְיוֹצְאָה, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֵינָהּ מְכוּרָה כׇּל עִיקָּר. מַאי טַעְמָא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל? קַל וָחוֹמֶר, וּמָה מְכוּרָה כְּבָר יוֹצְאָה, שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְכוּרָה אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא תִּימָּכֵר?

b6.he: וּלְרַב, לָא אָמְרִינַן קַל וָחוֹמֶר כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא? וְהָתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל יִמְכּוֹר אָדָם אֶת בִּתּוֹ כְּשֶׁהִיא נַעֲרָה? אָמַרְתָּ קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה מְכוּרָה כְּבָר — יוֹצְאָה עַכְשָׁיו, שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְכוּרָה — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא תִּימָּכֵר?

b7.he: הָתָם לָא הָדְרָא מִיזְדַּבְּנָא, הָכָא הָדְרָא מִיזְדַּבְּנָא.

b8.he: מֵיתִיבִי: ״אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל שָׁנִים תִּקְנֶה״ — מְלַמֵּד שֶׁמּוֹכְרִין סָמוּךְ לַיּוֹבֵל, מוּפְלָג מִן הַיּוֹבֵל מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לְפִי רֹב הַשָּׁנִים... וּלְפִי מְעוֹט הַשָּׁנִים״.

b9.he: וּבִשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל עַצְמָהּ לֹא יִמְכּוֹר, וְאִם מָכַר — אֵינָהּ מְכוּרָה! אָמַר לְךָ רַב: אֵינָהּ מְכוּרָה לְמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי תְבוּאוֹת, אֲבָל מְכוּרָה הִיא וְיוֹצְאָה.

b10.he: וְאִי אִיזְדַּבּוֹנֵי מִיזְדַּבְּנָה, תֵּיקוּם בִּרְשׁוּתֵיהּ עַד בָּתַר יוֹבֵל, וּבָתַר יוֹבֵל נֵיכְלַיהּ שְׁנֵי תְבוּאוֹת וְנַיהְדְּרַהּ! מִי לָא תַּנְיָא: אֲכָלָהּ שָׁנָה אַחַת לִפְנֵי הַיּוֹבֵל — מַשְׁלִימִין לוֹ שָׁנָה אַחֶרֶת אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל? הָתָם נָחֵית לַאֲכִילָה, הָכָא לָא נָחֵית לַאֲכִילָה.

b11.he: אָמַר רַב עָנָן: שְׁמַעִית מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל תַּרְתֵּי, חֲדָא הָךְ, וְאִידַּךְ הַמּוֹכֵר עַבְדּוֹ לְגוֹיִם אוֹ בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ יָצָא לְחֵירוּת.

b12.he: חֲדָא הָדְרִי זְבִינֵי, וַחֲדָא לָא הָדְרִי זְבִינֵי, וְלָא יָדַעְנָא הֵי (מיניה) [מִינַּיְהוּ].

b13.he: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: נִיחְזֵי אֲנַן, מִדְּתַנְיָא בְּבָרַיְיתָא: הַמּוֹכֵר עַבְדּוֹ בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ יָצָא לְחֵירוּת, וְצָרִיךְ גֵּט שִׁיחְרוּר מֵרַבּוֹ שֵׁנִי. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, מִדְּקָרֵי לֵיהּ לְשֵׁנִי ״רַבּוֹ״, אַלְמָא לָא הָדְרִי זְבִינֵי, וְכִי קָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכָא: אֵינָהּ מְכוּרָה וּמָעוֹת חוֹזְרִין.

messages.text: Continued from 28b: the mishna taught that priests’ dedications have no redemption and are given to the priests like teruma; Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says unspecified dedications are for Temple maintenance and the Rabbis say they are for the priests; and a person may dedicate even his sacrificial animals.
Gemara
Dedications of property for priests have no redemption, and one gives the property to the priest.

With regard to these dedications, as long as they remain in the house of the owner they are considered like consecrated property in every sense, as it is stated: “Every dedicated item is most sacred to the Lord” (Leviticus 27:28).

verse.he: אַךְ־כׇּל־חֵרֶם אֲשֶׁר יַחֲרִם אִישׁ לַיהֹוָה מִכׇּל־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ מֵאָדָם וּבְהֵמָה וּמִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ לֹא יִמָּכֵר וְלֹא יִגָּאֵל כׇּל־חֵרֶם קֹדֶשׁ־קׇדָשִׁים הוּא לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: But of all that anyone owns, be it human or animal or land-holding, nothing that has been proscribed for GOD may be sold or redeemed; every proscribed thing is totally consecrated to GOD.

notes.he: ויש בהן מעילה:
notes.en: Gemara. They are like consecrated property: and the prohibition of misuse [me’ila] applies to them.

notes.he: שאסורין בהנאה ומועלין בהן:
notes.en: They are like consecrated property in every respect: that they are forbidden for benefit, and the prohibition of misuse applies to them.

messages.text: Once the owner has given them to the priest they are in every sense like non-sacred property, as it is stated: “Everything dedicated in Israel shall be yours” (Numbers 18:14), i.e., it shall be like all other regular property belonging to a priest, which is non-sacred.

verse.en: Everything that has been proscribed in Israel shall be yours.

notes.he: כשאר ממונו של כהן:
notes.en: They are like non-sacred property: like the rest of the priest’s property.

notes.he: לך יהיה אפי' לקדש בהן את האשה ואין בהן מעילה:
notes.en: “Shall be yours”: even to betroth a woman with them, and the prohibition of misuse does not apply to them.

messages.text: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says dedications donated without specification are designated for Temple maintenance, as it is stated: “Every dedicated item is most sacred to the Lord” (Leviticus 27:28). And the Rabbis say they are designated for priests, as it is stated: “As a field dedicated; its possession shall be to the priest” (Leviticus 27:21), whereas the verse cited by Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira teaches that dedication takes effect on offerings of the most sacred order and offerings of lesser sanctity.
Granted, the opinion of the Rabbis is clear, as they explain their reason and the reason of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, i.e., they interpret the verse he cited as his proof.

notes.he: דמתניתין מפרשי טעמא וקרא דרבי יהודה כדקתני א"כ למה נאמר כל חרם כו':
notes.en: Granted, the Rabbis: of our mishna explain the reason, and [they explain] the verse of Rabbi Yehuda [ben Beteira], as it teaches: “If so, why is it stated: ‘Every dedicated item,’” and so on.

notes.he: דאמרי לכהן כדקא מפרשי טעמא דידהו קרא דידהו וקרא דר' יהודה בן בתירא לדרשא]:
notes.en: [Granted, the Rabbis: who say [unspecified dedications are] for the priest, as they explain their reason, their own verse, and the verse of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, for an exposition.]

messages.text: But as for Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, this verse: “As a field dedicated; its possession shall be to the priest,” what does he do with it, i.e., what does he derive from it?

verse.he: וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: when it is released in the jubilee, the land shall be holy to GOD, as land proscribed; it becomes the priest’s holding.

notes.dh: אלא לרבי יהודה כשדה החרם למאי אתא
notes.he: ולחרמי כהנים כדמפרש ליכא לאוקמי דמכל חרם לך יהיה נפקא:
notes.en: But according to Rabbi Yehuda, what does “As a field dedicated” come for? And it cannot be established as referring to priests’ dedications, as [the Rabbis] explain it, for [according to him] that is derived from “Everything dedicated… shall be yours.”

messages.text: The verse is necessary for him for that which is taught in a baraita that discusses the case of one who consecrated his ancestral field and failed to redeem it. This field becomes the possession of the priests at the Jubilee Year.
messages.quote: this verse: “As a field dedicated”, what does he do with it

messages.text: Why must the verse state at its end: “As a field dedicated; its possession shall be to the priest”?

notes.he: כשדה החרם לכהן תהיה אחוזתו מה ת"ל לימא קדש לה' ולכהן תהיה מה ת"ל שדה חרם (ואחוזתו):
notes.en: “As a field dedicated; its possession shall be to the priest”: why does the verse state it? Let it say “sacred to the Lord” and “it shall be to the priest”; why does the verse state “a dedicated field” (and “his possession”)?

messages.text: From where is it derived with regard to a priest who consecrated his dedicated field, i.e., a field that was dedicated by an Israelite and was given to him and he then consecrated it, and then the Jubilee Year arrived, that he may not say: Since a field that was consecrated by its owners and was not redeemed goes out of the owner’s possession and passes to the possession of the priests at the Jubilee Year, and this field that I consecrated is already in my possession, it is therefore mine.

notes.he: שדה שהחרים ישראל והגיע לחלק כהן שדה שלא יאמר הואיל וכשיגיע יובל אם לא אפדנה אני מיד גזבר ויגאלנה אחר תתחלק לכהנים ביובל כדין מקדיש שדה אחוזה דהא שדה חרם לגבי כהן אחוזה היא כדכתיב כשדה החרם לכהן תהיה אחוזתו ועכשיו שאני מוחזק בה תהא שלי שהרי דין הוא בשל אחרים אני זוכה אם היה ישראל מקדיש שדה אחוזתו כשיגיע יובל תתחלק לי בשל עצמי לא כל שכן:
notes.en: Who consecrated his dedicated field: a field that an Israelite dedicated and that came into the portion of a priest. That he may not say: Since, when the Jubilee arrives, if I do not redeem it from the treasurer and another redeems it, it will be divided among the priests at the Jubilee, as is the law of one who consecrates an ancestral field (for a dedicated field is, for the priest, an ancestral field, as it is written: “As a field dedicated; its possession shall be to the priest”), then now that I hold it, let it be mine. For it is logical: with the property of others I acquire, since if an Israelite consecrated his ancestral field, when the Jubilee arrives it is divided to me; with my own, all the more so?

messages.text: And this claim of the priest is based on logical inference: If I acquire the fields of others that were consecrated and not redeemed at the Jubilee Year, then with regard to my own property, all the more so is it not clear that I should acquire it?

Therefore, the verse states, with regard to an ancestral field that one consecrated: “As a field dedicated; its possession shall be to the priest,” which teaches that this priest does not acquire the field.

notes.he: דהאי קרא במקדיש שדה אחוזה כתיב:
notes.en: The verse states: “As a field dedicated,” and so on: for this verse is written about one who consecrates an ancestral field.

messages.text: But what have we now learned about a consecrated ancestral field from a dedicated field? In other words, the verse, which is dealing with an ancestral field, says an ancestral field is like a dedicated field, but it does not explicitly state the halakha of dedicated fields.

notes.he: על שדה אחוזה כו' מה שדה אחוזה שהקדיש ישראל וגאלה אחד מן הכהנים תצא מידו ביובל ותתחלק לכל בני המשמר כדאמר בפירקין דלעיל אחוזתו שלו ואין זו שלו אף שדה חרמו כו':
notes.en: What have we learned from the dedicated field: about the ancestral field, and so on. Just as an ancestral field that an Israelite consecrated and one of the priests redeemed goes out of his hand at the Jubilee and is divided among all the members of the watch, as is said above in our chapter: “his ancestral possession,” his own, and this is not his own [25b], so too his dedicated field, and so on.

messages.text: Rather, this case of a dedicated field comes to teach a halakha about an ancestral field but is found to derive a halakha from that case, i.e., the verse juxtaposes a dedicated field of a priest to the ancestral field of an Israelite.

Just as the ancestral field of an Israelite, which was redeemed by a priest from the Temple treasury, goes out of his possession at the arrival of the Jubilee Year and is divided among all the priests of the watch serving at the beginning of the Jubilee Year (see 25b), so too, the dedicated field of a priest that remained in his possession goes out of his possession and is divided among his brothers, the priests of the watch serving at the beginning of the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: שדה שהחרים ישראל ויצא לכהן והקדישו כהן שלא יאמר הואיל ויוצא לכהנים ביובל דהאי כהן מקדיש שדה חרמו הוי כאילו הקדיש שדה אחוזה ודין הוא מה שדה אחוזה של ישראל שיצאה ביובל וגאלה אחד מן הכהנים יוצאה מתחת ידו ומתחלקת לכל הכהנים כדאמר לעיל בפירקין אחוזתו שלו ואין זה שלו אף מקדיש שדה חרמו נמי מתחלקת לאחיו הכהנים:
notes.en: [His dedicated field: a field that an Israelite dedicated and that went out to a priest, and the priest consecrated it. That he may not say: Since it goes out to the priests at the Jubilee [it is mine]. For this priest who consecrates his dedicated field is as if he consecrated an ancestral field. And it is logical: just as an Israelite’s ancestral field that went out at the Jubilee, which one of the priests redeemed, goes out from under his hand and is divided among all the priests, as it says above in our chapter: “his ancestral possession,” his own, and this one is not his own, so too one who consecrates his dedicated field: it too is divided among his brothers the priests.]

messages.text: And the other, i.e., the Rabbis, from where do they derive this halakha?

They derive it from a superfluous term in the verse, as it could have stated merely: Dedicated [ḥerem], from which one would have derived that unspecified dedications are designated for the priests. Yet the verse actually states: “Haḥerem,” with the definite article, and therefore both halakhot are derived from this verse.

notes.he: רבנן נפקא להו הא מה"א דהחרם]:
notes.en: And the other: the Rabbis derive this from the [extra] heh of “haḥerem.”]

messages.text: And as for the other, Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, he does not learn anything from the difference between ḥerem and haḥerem. Accordingly, he derives from here only that if a priest consecrated his dedicated field it is removed from his possession.

And as for Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, from where does he derive that a dedication takes effect on offerings of the most sacred order and offerings of lesser sanctity, which, according to the Rabbis, is learned from the verse: “Every dedicated item is most sacred to the Lord” (Leviticus 27:28)?
He holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael, who derives this halakha from another source, as explained in the mishna below.

notes.he: דמפיק לה במתניתין מיקדיש ואל תקדיש:
notes.en: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael: who derives it in the mishna [below] from “you shall consecrate” and “do not consecrate.”

notes.he: כלומר נפקא ליה דחל על קדשי קדשים ועל קדשים קלים מהיכא דנפקא ליה לר' ישמעאל כדתנן ר' ישמעאל אומר כתוב אחד אומר תקדיש דכתיב כל הבכור אשר יולד תקדיש וגו' וכתוב אחד אמר אל תקדיש דכתיב אך בכור אשר יבוכר לה' (לכהן) [בבהמה] לא יקדיש איש אותו הא כיצד מקדישו אתה הקדש עילוי כדאמרן אם נדר נותן את דמיהן ואם נדבה נותן (טובתן) [טובת הנאה] לבדק הבית דהיינו הקדש עילוי לדמיו ואי אתה מקדישו הקדש מזבח לשם זבח אחר וגלי רחמנא בקדשים קלים [כגון בכור דחל על קדשים קלים] וה"ה לקדשי קדשים שחל עליהם חרם להקדש עילוי כדאמרן:
notes.en: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael: that is, he derives that it takes effect on offerings of the most sacred order and on offerings of lesser sanctity from where Rabbi Yishmael derives it, as we learned [in the mishna]: Rabbi Yishmael says: One verse says “you shall consecrate,” as it is written: “All the firstborn that is born… you shall consecrate,” and so on; and one verse says “do not consecrate,” as it is written: “However, the firstborn that is born first to the Lord among animals, a man shall not consecrate it.” How so? You consecrate it with a consecration of value, as we said: if it was a vow, he gives their value, and if a gift offering, he gives the benefit of discretion to Temple maintenance, which is a consecration of value for its worth; and you do not consecrate it with a consecration for the altar, for the sake of another offering. The Merciful One revealed this with offerings of lesser sanctity [such as a firstborn: that it takes effect on offerings of lesser sanctity], and the same is true of offerings of the most sacred order, that a dedication takes effect on them as a consecration of value, as we said.

messages.text: § The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira that unspecified dedications of property are designated for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: דסתם חרמים לבדק הבית:
notes.en: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira: that unspecified dedications are for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: דאמר סתם חרמים לבדק הבית:
notes.en: [The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda: who said unspecified dedications are for Temple maintenance.

messages.text: And would Rav leave aside the majority opinion of the Rabbis and act in accordance with the individual opinion of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira?
messages.quote: in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira

messages.text: This dispute is taught in a baraita in the opposite manner, i.e., it is the Rabbis who hold that unspecified dedications are designated for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: דרבנן אמרי לבדק הבית ורבי יהודה לכהנים:
notes.en: The baraita is taught the opposite way: that the Rabbis say [unspecified dedications are] for Temple maintenance, and Rabbi Yehuda [ben Beteira says they are] for the priests.

notes.he: הואיל דההוא דר' יהודה מוקים לה כרבנן]:
notes.en: The baraita is taught the opposite way: since it establishes that [opinion] of Rabbi Yehuda as that of the Rabbis.]

messages.text: Would Rav leave aside a mishna and act in accordance with a baraita?
Rav teaches the mishna as well in the opposite manner, in accordance with the baraita.

notes.he: מתניתין נמי איפכא תנא הואיל ותני ברייתא איפכא:
notes.en: He teaches the mishna the opposite way as well: since he teaches the baraita the opposite way.

messages.text: What did you see that you chose to reverse the opinions in the mishna due to the baraita? Let us reverse the opinions in the baraita due to the mishna.
Rav learned by tradition from his teachers that the opinions cited in the mishna should be reversed.

notes.he: מרביה דרביה אגמריה דמתני' משבשתא היא:
notes.en: Rav learned it by tradition: from his teacher; his teacher’s teacher taught him that the mishna is a corrupted text.

notes.he: רב גמריה גמיר דאתנייה רביה לברייתא איפכא:
notes.en: Rav learned it by tradition: for his teacher taught it to him [as] the baraita [has it], reversed.

messages.text: If so, why does Rav state that the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira? He should have said it is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis.

notes.he: כיון דאפיך דר' יהודה כרבנן הלכה כרבנן איבעי ליה למימר:
notes.en: [If so: since he reversed [the opinion] of Rabbi Yehuda to be that of the Rabbis, he should have said the halakha is in accordance with the Rabbis.

messages.text: This is what Rav is saying: In accordance with the manner in which you reversed the opinions and taught them in the mishna, the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira.

notes.he: לדידי האי דאמריתהו משמיה דר' יהודה גמירנא לה משמא דרבנן לדידכו מאי דאפכיתו ותניתו בר' יהודה דלבדק הבית הלכה כר' יהודה]:
notes.en: This is what he is saying: For me, this that I stated in the name of Rabbi Yehuda, I learned it in the name of the Rabbis; [but] for you, according to what you reversed and teach as Rabbi Yehuda’s, that [unspecified dedications are] for Temple maintenance, the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.]

messages.text: § There was a certain man who dedicated his property in Pumbedita. He came before Rav Yehuda to ask him what to do.

Take four dinars and desacralize the dedicated property by transferring its sanctity onto them. And then throw the dinars into the river, because one may not derive benefit from them. And then the property will be permitted to you, as it will have been redeemed.

notes.he: לד' זוזי בנהרא דהקדש הן לבדק הבית דאי לכהן לית להו פדיון ולכהן בעי מיתבינהו:
notes.en: And throw them: the four dinars, into the river, for they are consecrated to Temple maintenance. For if [the property were] for a priest, there would be no redemption for it, and it would have to be given to a priest.

notes.dh: שקול ד' זוזי ואחיל עלייהו ושדינהו בנהרא ולישתרי לך
notes.he: ואם תאמר והא אמר בפרק קמא דע"ז (דף יג. ושם) אין מקדישין ואין מחרימין ואין מעריכין בזמן הזה ואם הקדיש והחרים והעריך בהמה תעקר פירות וכלים ירקבו והכא בזמן הזה איירי כדמסיק הכא ואמאי לא אמרי' ירקבו וצ"ל דדוקא במטלטלין קאמר דירקבו דלא אתי בהו לידי תקלה אם ממתינים עד שירקבו והכא במקרקעי איירי דאם ימתין (לאו) אתי לידי תקלה והכי נמי איתא בסמוך דאמר והא מעשה דפומבדיתא מקרקעי היה:
notes.en: Take four dinars and desacralize [the property] onto them, and throw them into the river, and it will be permitted to you: And if you say: But it says in the first chapter of Avoda Zara (13a): One does not consecrate, dedicate or pledge valuations in the present time, and if one consecrated, dedicated or pledged a valuation, an animal is hamstrung, and produce and vessels are left to rot. And here it is speaking of the present time, as it concludes here; so why do we not say they are left to rot? One must say that it says they are left to rot specifically of movable property, which does not lead to a stumbling block [i.e., misuse] if one waits until it rots. But here it is speaking of land, where, if one waits, it leads to a stumbling block. And so too it is found shortly after, where it says: “But that incident in Pumbedita was land.”

notes.he: משום דקסבר סתם חרמים לבדק הבית וכיון דליכא בהמ"ק לית ליה תקנה אלא בפדיון ולמישדי בנהרא:
notes.en: And throw them into the river, and it will be permitted to you: because he holds unspecified dedications are for Temple maintenance, and since there is no Temple, there is no remedy except redemption and throwing [the money] into the river.

messages.text: Evidently, Rav Yehuda holds that unspecified dedications of property are designated for Temple maintenance, which is why the man could redeem his property. Had the property been designated for the priests there could be no redemption, as taught in the mishna.
In accordance with whose opinion does Rav Yehuda hold, when he told the man to desacralize the dedicated property by transferring its sanctity onto money worth less than the dedicated property?
messages.quote: Take four dinars and desacralize the dedicated property

messages.text: He holds in accordance with the opinion of Shmuel,
Consecrated property worth one hundred dinars that one desacralized onto an item worth one peruta is desacralized.
One can say that Shmuel said this is the halakha only in a case where one already desacralized the property, i.e., after the fact. Did he say one may do so ab initio?
messages.quote: that one desacralized onto an item worth one peruta is desacralized

messages.text: This matter, that one must desacralize consecrated property onto an item worth the value of the property ab initio, applies only during a period when the Temple is standing, as there is a loss caused to the Temple treasury by desacralizing its property onto an item worth less than its value. But in the present time, when the Temple is not standing and there is no Temple treasury, one may desacralize with an item worth less than the consecrated property even ab initio.

notes.he: דליכא בית וליכא פסידא אלא איסורא הוא דרביעא עלייהו אפילו לכתחלה נמי:
notes.en: In the present time: when there is no Temple and there is no loss, but only a prohibition rests on them, even ab initio as well.

notes.he: לא הוה שרי למיפרקי לכתחלה אלא בשיוויו משום פסידא דהקדש]:
notes.en: [This applies when the Temple is standing: it would not be permitted to redeem it ab initio except at its value, because of the loss to the Temple treasury.]

messages.text: If so, then one may even desacralize with one peruta as well. Why, then, did Rav Yehuda require the man to use four dinars?
He required four dinars in order to publicize the matter, so that the community will know the property is permitted for use only because it was redeemed.

notes.he: משום פרסומי מלתא דבר פדייה הוא הוא דאצרכיה ד' זוזי דחשיבי אבל מ"מ בפרוטה סגיא כדשמואל:
notes.en: To publicize the matter that it is redeemed property: that is why he required four dinars, which are significant; but in any case a peruta suffices, as Shmuel [said].

messages.text: If I had been there when this man asked what to do, I would have given all of the property to the priests.

notes.he: [יהיבנא כולהו לכהנים אלמא קסבר סתם חרמים לכהנים וכיון דאיכא כהנים חרמי כהנים אין להן פדיון]:
notes.en: [I would have given all of it to the priests: evidently he holds unspecified dedications are for the priests, and since there are priests, priests’ dedications have no redemption.]

messages.text: Evidently, Ulla holds that unspecified dedications of property are designated for the priests, and therefore they cannot be redeemed.
messages.quote: I would have given all of the property to the priests

messages.text: It can be inferred from the previous discussion that the halakhot of dedications are in effect even today. The Gemara raises an objection to this opinion from a baraita:

The sale of a Hebrew slave is practiced only during a period when the Jubilee Year is observed, as it is stated: “And if your brother be waxen poor with you, and sell himself to you…he shall serve with you until the year of Jubilee” (Leviticus 25:39–40).

verse.he: וְכִי־יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ וְנִמְכַּר־לָךְ לֹא־תַעֲבֹד בּוֹ עֲבֹדַת עָבֶד׃ כְּשָׂכִיר כְּתוֹשָׁב יִהְיֶה עִמָּךְ עַד־שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל יַעֲבֹד עִמָּךְ׃
verse.en: If your kin under you continue in straits and must be given over to you, do not subject them to the treatment of a slave. Remaining with you as a hired or bound laborer, they shall serve with you only until the jubilee year.

notes.he: דאינו נמכר בזמן הזה:
notes.en: A Hebrew slave is practiced only: that he is not sold in the present time.

messages.text: And likewise the halakhot pertaining to a dedicated, i.e., ancestral, field apply only during a period that the Jubilee Year is observed, as it is stated: “Then that which he has sold shall remain in the hand of him that has bought…and in the Jubilee it shall go out, and he shall return to his possession” (Leviticus 25:28).

verse.he: וְאִם לֹא־מָצְאָה יָדוֹ דֵּי הָשִׁיב לוֹ וְהָיָה מִמְכָּרוֹ בְּיַד הַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ עַד שְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל וְיָצָא בַּיֹּבֵל וְשָׁב לַאֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃ {ס}
verse.en: If [the seller] lacks sufficient means to recover it, what was sold shall remain with the purchaser until the jubilee; in the jubilee year it shall be released, so that they return to their holding.

notes.he: דין שדה אחוזה שתהא נגאלת בגירוע אלא אם ירצה הלוקח להחזירה לו בדמים שירצה מחזיר ואם לאו אין כופין אותו וכן דין מקדיש שדה אחוזה בזמן הבית ואין היובל נוהג כגון משגלו שבט ראובן וגד שבטלו היובלות אין נגאלת אלא בשויה:
notes.en: And an ancestral field does not [Rashi’s text reads “ancestral field”; the printed Gemara reads “dedicated field”]: the law of an ancestral field, that it is redeemed with a deduction [for the years the buyer has had it, does not apply]. Rather, if the buyer wishes to return it to him for whatever money he wishes, he returns it, and if not, one does not compel him. And likewise the law of one who consecrates an ancestral field at a time when the Temple stands but the Jubilee is not in force, such as after the tribes of Reuben and Gad were exiled, when the Jubilees ceased: it is redeemed only at its value.

messages.text: Finally, the halakhot pertaining to houses of walled cities apply only during a period when the Jubilee Year is observed, as it is stated: “Then the house that is in the walled city shall be made sure in perpetuity to him that bought it, throughout his generations; it shall not go out in the Jubilee” (Leviticus 25:30).

verse.he: וְאִם לֹא־יִגָּאֵל עַד־מְלֹאת לוֹ שָׁנָה תְמִימָה וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר־בָּעִיר אֲשֶׁר־[לוֹ] (לא) חֹמָה לַצְּמִיתֻת לַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ לְדֹרֹתָיו לֹא יֵצֵא בַּיֹּבֵל׃
verse.en: If it is not redeemed before a full year has elapsed, the house in the walled city shall pass to the purchaser beyond reclaim throughout the ages; it shall not be released in the jubilee.

notes.he: דלא כייפינן ליה ללוקח אם בא מוכר לגאלה אפילו בתוך שנה:
notes.en: Houses of walled cities are not practiced: for we do not compel the buyer if the seller comes to redeem it, even within the year.

messages.text: The halakhot pertaining to a dedicated field apply only during a period when the Jubilee Year is observed, as it is stated: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be sacred to the Lord, as a field dedicated; its possession shall be to the priest” (Leviticus 27:21).

verse.he: וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: when it is released in the jubilee, the land shall be holy to GOD, as land proscribed; it becomes the priest’s holding.

notes.he: ר"ש [אומר] מהכא דאין שדה חרמים נוהג אלא בזמן היובל אבל מטלטלי אפילו בזמן הזה:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon [says]: from here [we learn] that [the law of] dedicated fields is practiced only at a time when the Jubilee is in force, but movable property [is affected] even in the present time.

messages.text: The halakhot pertaining to a gentile who resides in Eretz Yisrael and observes the seven Noahide mitzvot [ger toshav] apply only during a period when the Jubilee Year is observed.

notes.he: שיהא ישראל מצווה להחיותו. גר תושב שקיבל עליו שלא לעבוד עבודת כוכבים ואוכל נבילות:
notes.en: A ger toshav is not practiced: [in the sense] that a Jew is commanded to sustain him. A ger toshav is one who accepted upon himself not to worship idols, and who eats carcasses [i.e., meat not slaughtered according to halakha].

messages.text: What is the reason? It is derived from a verbal analogy between “well” and “well.” It is written here, with regard to a Hebrew slave, who can be sold only when the Jubilee Year is observed: “Because he fares well with you” (Deuteronomy 15:16).
messages.quote: ger toshav apply only during a period when the Jubilee Year is observed

verse.he: וְהָיָה כִּי־יֹאמַר אֵלֶיךָ לֹא אֵצֵא מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אֲהֵבְךָ וְאֶת־בֵּיתֶךָ כִּי־טוֹב לוֹ עִמָּךְ׃
verse.en: But should they say to you, “I do not want to leave you”—for they love you and your household and are happy with you—

messages.text: And it is written there, with regard to a ger toshav: “Where it is well for him; you shall not wrong him” (Deuteronomy 23:17).

verse.he: עִמְּךָ יֵשֵׁב בְּקִרְבְּךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ בַּטּוֹב לוֹ לֹא תּוֹנֶנּוּ׃ {ס}
verse.en: He shall live with you in any place he may choose among the settlements in your midst, wherever he pleases; you must not ill-treat him.

notes.he: בעבד עברי כי טוב לו עמך וכתיב בגר תושב עמך ישב וגו' דלא תסגיר עבד אל אדוניו בגר תושב משתעי דהכי מוקמינן לה במסכת גיטין בפ' השולח גט (דף מה.) וכתיב בתריה עמך ישב בקרבך וגו'. מכל מקום לתרוייהו קשיא דקתני אין שדה חרמים נוהג אלא בזמן יובל:
notes.en: It is written: of a Hebrew slave, “Because he fares well with you,” and it is written of a ger toshav: “He shall dwell with you,” and so on. For “You shall not deliver a slave to his master” speaks of a ger toshav, as we establish it in tractate Gittin, in the chapter HaSholeiaḥ Get (45a), and after it is written: “He shall dwell with you, in your midst,” and so on. In any case, it is difficult for both of them [Rav Yehuda and Ulla], since it teaches: The [law of a] dedicated field is practiced only at a time when the Jubilee is in force.

notes.he: שמצווין להחיותו ומוזהרין על הונאתו. גר תושב זה הכופר בעבודת כוכבים וכתיב נמי גבי גר תושב בטוב לו לא תוננו דהאי בטוב לו בלא תסגיר עבד אל אדוניו [כתי'] ומפרש בסיפרי זה גר תושב:
notes.en: A ger toshav is not practiced: that we are commanded to sustain him and are warned against wronging him. A ger toshav is one who renounces idol worship. And it is also written of a ger toshav: “Where it is well for him; you shall not wrong him,” for this “where it is well for him” is written in [the passage of] “You shall not deliver a slave to his master,” and the Sifrei explains: this is a ger toshav.

messages.text: The objection is that it is evident from the baraita that the halakhot pertaining to dedicated fields apply only when the Jubilee Year is observed.

messages.caption: What the baraita says applies only when the Jubilee is observed, and the verse each opinion cites

messages.text: It is not difficult. This baraita is discussing the halakha with regard to land, whereas that incident, in Pumbedita, in which a dedication was effected, occurred with movable property.

notes.he: אין נוהגין כדכתיב בצאתו ביובל כשדה החרם:
notes.en: Land: is not practiced, as it is written: “When it goes out in the Jubilee… as a field dedicated.”

notes.dh: [שמעינן מהכא דאין שדה חרמים נוהג אלא בזמן היובל ואמאי אצרכיה רב יהודה פדייה
notes.he: לא קשיא מקרקעי אין נוהגין אלא בזמן היובל אבל מטלטלי אפי' בזמן הזה]:
notes.en: [We learn from here that [the law of] dedicated fields is practiced only at a time when the Jubilee is in force; so why did Rav Yehuda require redemption? It is not difficult: land [is affected] only at a time when the Jubilee is in force, but movable property even in the present time.]

messages.text: But that incident that occurred in Pumbedita involved land as well, and Rav Yehuda nevertheless required the man to redeem them.

notes.he: והא מעשה דפומבדיתא במקרקעי נמי הוה דהאמר דאחרימנהו לכולהו נכסי בין מקרקעי בין מטלטלי:
notes.en: But the incident in Pumbedita was also with land: for it says he dedicated all his property, both land and movable property.

messages.text: Land outside of Eretz Yisrael is considered like movable property in Eretz Yisrael.

notes.dh: מקרקעי דחוצה לארץ כמטלטלי דא"י דמו
notes.he: והא אמרינן דבמטלטלי נוהג אפי' בזמן הזה:
notes.en: Land outside the Land [of Israel] is considered like movable property in the Land of Israel: and we said that with movable property it is practiced even in the present time.

messages.text: Mishna
One verse states: “All the firstborn males that are born of your herd and of your flock you shall consecrate to the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 15:19),

verse.he: כׇּל־הַבְּכוֹר אֲשֶׁר יִוָּלֵד בִּבְקָרְךָ וּבְצֹאנְךָ הַזָּכָר תַּקְדִּישׁ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תַעֲבֹד בִּבְכֹר שׁוֹרֶךָ וְלֹא תָגֹז בְּכוֹר צֹאנֶךָ׃
verse.en: You shall consecrate to the ETERNAL your God all male firstlings that are born in your herd and in your flock: you must not work your firstling ox or shear your firstling sheep.

notes.he: כדמפרשינן לעיל]:
notes.en: [A person may dedicate his sacrificial animals, and so on: as we explained above.] [Rabbeinu Gershom here cites the opening words of this part of the mishna on 28b.]

notes.he: רבי ישמעאל אומר כתוב אחד כו' דר' ישמעאל יליף להו מהני קראי דחל על קדשי קדשים ועל קדשים קלים כדמפרשינן לעיל:
notes.en: Rabbi Yishmael says: One verse, and so on: for Rabbi Yishmael derives from these verses that it takes effect on offerings of the most sacred order and on offerings of lesser sanctity, as we explained above.

notes.he: גבי בכור דכתיב כל הבכור [וגו'] תקדיש (דברים טו):
notes.en: Mishna. One verse says “you shall consecrate”: regarding a firstborn, as it is written: “All the firstborn [and so on] you shall consecrate” (Deuteronomy 15).

messages.text: and one verse states: “However, the firstborn among animals that is born first to the Lord, a man shall not consecrate it” (Leviticus 27:26).

verse.he: אַךְ־בְּכוֹר אֲשֶׁר־יְבֻכַּר לַיהֹוָה בִּבְהֵמָה לֹא־יַקְדִּישׁ אִישׁ אֹתוֹ אִם־שׁוֹר אִם־שֶׂה לַיהֹוָה הוּא׃
verse.en: A firstling of animals, however, which—as a firstling—is GOD’s, cannot be consecrated by anybody; whether ox or sheep, it is GOD’s.

notes.he: אך בכור אשר יבוכר לה' בבהמה לא יקדיש איש אותו וגו' (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״ו):
notes.en: And one verse says “shall not consecrate”: “However, the firstborn among animals that is born first to the Lord, a man shall not consecrate it,” and so on (Leviticus 27:26).

messages.text: It is impossible to say: “You shall consecrate,” as it is already stated: “A man shall not consecrate.” It is likewise impossible to say: “A man shall not consecrate,” as it is already stated: “You shall consecrate.”

How, then, can these verses be reconciled? You can consecrate the firstborn animal by a consecration of value, i.e., an individual can donate to the Temple treasury the amount he would be willing to pay for the right to give the firstborn to a specific priest; and you cannot consecrate it by a consecration for the altar, as a firstborn may not be sacrificed for the sake of any other offering.

notes.he: להעלותו בדמים ויתן טובת הנאתו לכהן:
notes.en: A consecration of value: to raise it in monetary value, and he gives its benefit of discretion to the priest [i.e., what is consecrated is the money value of the owner’s right to choose the priest, as in the mishna on 28b].

notes.he: פי' להעלותו בדמים ליתן טובת הנאה לכהן:
notes.en: A consecration of value: meaning, to raise it in monetary value, to give the benefit of discretion to the priest.

notes.he: שיהא שם זבח אחר חל עליו:
notes.en: And you cannot consecrate it as a consecration for the altar: that the name of another offering should take effect on it.

messages.text: Gemara

And the Rabbis, who derive the halakha that a dedication takes effect on all offerings of sanctity from the verse: “Every dedicated item is most sacred to the Lord” (Leviticus 27:28), would explain that the verse “A man shall not consecrate” is necessary to teach that there is a Torah prohibition against consecrating a firstborn animal for the sake of another offering.
messages.quote: a man shall not consecrate it

notes.he: דנפקא להו הך דרשא (לעיל ערכין כח:) מכל חרם קדש קדשים:
notes.en: Gemara. And the Rabbis: who derive that exposition (above, 28b) from “Every dedicated item is most sacred.”

notes.he: דלא ילפי לה מהני קראי [הני קראי] למאי מיבעי להו:
notes.en: And the Rabbis: who do not derive it from these verses, what do they need [these verses] for?

notes.he: שאם מתפיסו לשם זבח אחר עובר בלאו:
notes.en: “Do not consecrate” is needed for a prohibition: that if he designates it for the sake of another offering, he transgresses a prohibition.

notes.he: דכתיב לא יקדיש איש אותו מיבעי ליה למיקם עליה בלאו אם מקדישו לזבח אחר]:
notes.en: [“Do not consecrate”: as it is written: “A man shall not consecrate it,” is needed to make him liable for a prohibition if he consecrates it for another offering.]

messages.text: As for the other verse discussed in the mishna: “You shall consecrate,” it is necessary for that which is taught in a baraita:

From where is it derived with regard to a firstborn animal that was born in one’s flock that it is a mitzva to consecrate it verbally as a firstborn? As it is stated: “The firstborn males that are born of your herd and of your flock you shall consecrate.”

verse.he: כׇּל־הַבְּכוֹר אֲשֶׁר יִוָּלֵד בִּבְקָרְךָ וּבְצֹאנְךָ הַזָּכָר תַּקְדִּישׁ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תַעֲבֹד בִּבְכֹר שׁוֹרֶךָ וְלֹא תָגֹז בְּכוֹר צֹאנֶךָ׃
verse.en: You shall consecrate to the ETERNAL your God all male firstlings that are born in your herd and in your flock: you must not work your firstling ox or shear your firstling sheep.

notes.he: לשם בכור ואף על פי שהוא קדוש מאליו:
notes.en: That it is a mitzva to consecrate it: for the sake of a firstborn, even though it is sacred on its own.

notes.he: שמצוה להקדישו לשם בכור:
notes.en: “You shall consecrate” is needed: that it is a mitzva to consecrate it for the sake of a firstborn.

messages.text: If one does not consecrate it verbally, is the animal not consecrated? It certainly is consecrated, as its sanctity is from the womb.
messages.lead: And Rabbi Yishmael, who maintains there is no such mitzva, would argue:
messages.quote: a mitzva to consecrate it verbally as a firstborn

notes.he: אמר לך אי לא מקדיש ליה לא קדיש בתמיה:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yishmael: says to you: If he does not consecrate it, is it not consecrated? [Said] in astonishment.

notes.he: ור' ישמעאל אמר לך להכי לא מיבעי דבכור ממילא קדיש דקדושתו מרחם אלא לא אתא קרא אלא לכדאמרן:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yishmael says to you: it is not needed for this, for a firstborn is consecrated on its own, as its sanctity is from the womb; rather, the verse comes only for what we said.

messages.text: And since when one does not consecrate it the animal is nevertheless sanctified automatically, he does not need to consecrate it verbally.

notes.he: ולית ליה לרבי ישמעאל הך דרשא:
notes.en: He does not need to consecrate it: and Rabbi Yishmael does not accept this exposition.

notes.he: ור' ישמעאל ההוא קרא דכל חרם [קדש] דרבנן ילפי מיניה שחל על קדשי קדשים [חרמים לבדק הבית שנאמר כל חרם קדש] ועל קדשים קלים מאי עביד ליה:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yishmael: that verse, “Every dedicated item is [most] sacred,” from which the Rabbis derive that it takes effect on offerings of the most sacred order [dedications for Temple maintenance, as it is stated: “Every dedicated item is most sacred”] and on offerings of lesser sanctity, what does he do with it? [This question and the answer in the next note are not in the printed Gemara.]

notes.he: ר' ישמעאל סבר לה כר' יהודה בן בתירא דדריש לההוא קרא כל חרם קדש קדשים דסתם חרמים לבדק הבית [שנאמר כל חרם קדש קדשים הוא לה']:
notes.en: Rabbi Yishmael holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, who expounds that verse, “Every dedicated item is most sacred,” [to teach] that unspecified dedications are for Temple maintenance [as it is stated: “Every dedicated item is most sacred to the Lord”].

notes.he: הדרן עלך המקדיש
notes.en: We will return to you, [chapter] HaMakdish.

messages.text: הדרן עלך המקדיש שדהו · Hadran alakh HaMakdish Sadehu: we will return to you, chapter 8, “One Who Consecrates His Field.”
Chapter 9 · המוכר שדהו · HaMokher Sadehu, the last chapter of the tractate: selling an ancestral field and redeeming it, the Jubilee, and houses in walled cities.
Mishna

One who sells his field during a period when the Jubilee Year is in effect is not permitted to redeem it less than two years after the sale, as it is stated: “According to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you” (Leviticus 25:15). The plural form “years” indicates a minimum of two years.

verse.he: בְּמִסְפַּר שָׁנִים אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל תִּקְנֶה מֵאֵת עֲמִיתֶךָ בְּמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי־תְבוּאֹת יִמְכׇּר־לָךְ׃
verse.en: In buying from your neighbor, you shall deduct only for the number of years since the jubilee; and in selling to you, you shall be charged only for the remaining crop years:

notes.he: בזמן שהיובל נוהג:
notes.en: Mishna. One who sells, at the time of the Jubilee: when the Jubilee is in force.

notes.he: בזמן שהיובל נוהג:
notes.en: [At the time of the Jubilee: when the Jubilee is in force.

notes.he: אבל לאחר שתי שנים אם רוצה לפדותה פודה בעל כרחו של לוקח ונותן לו לפי מה שמכרה כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ה:כ״ז) וחשב את שני ממכרו שמחשב כמה שנים משמכרה עד היובל ומחלק הדמים לפי השנים כגון אם מכרה קודם היובל עשר שנים בעשר ליטרין נמצא שמכר פירות של כל שנה ושנה בליטרא שהרי סתם מכירה אינה אלא עד היובל הלכך אם שהתה ביד לוקח ה' שנים ואח"כ בא מוכר לגאלה מנכה לו לוקח ה' ליטרין ליטרא לכל שנה שאכלה שכך עלה חשבון כשיוצא מתחילה:
notes.en: Less than two years: but after two years, if he wishes to redeem it, he redeems it against the buyer’s will and gives him according to what he sold it for, as it is written: “Then let him count the years of its sale” (Leviticus 25:27). He calculates how many years there were from when he sold it until the Jubilee and divides the money according to the years. For example, if he sold it ten years before the Jubilee for ten litra, it emerges that he sold the produce of each year for a litra, for an unspecified sale is only until the Jubilee. Therefore, if it remained in the buyer’s hand five years and afterward the seller comes to redeem it, the buyer deducts five litra for him, a litra for each year that he consumed it, for that is how the reckoning came out at the start.

notes.he: שדהו מיד הלוקח עד לאחר ב' שנים למכירתו:
notes.en: He is not permitted to redeem: his field from the buyer until after two years from its sale.

notes.dh: שנא' במספר שני תבואות ימכר לך
notes.he: כלומר שתהא ברשות הלוקח ב' שנים (ואם) [או] יותר וכשהוא גואלה מחשב הדמים שנתן לו הלוקח בשביל השדה כנגד השנים שמשעת המכירה ועד היובל וכמה שמגיע לכל השנה מן הדמים כן ינכה לו הלוקח למוכר לפי השנים שהיתה ברשות הלוקח שנאמר וחשב המוכר את שני ממכרו שהיתה ברשות הלוקח ולפיהן ינכה מדמי גאולתו לפי חשבון דמי השנים ויחזור לו המותר מן הדמים ויקבל שדהו דכתיב והשיב את העודף לאיש אשר מכר לו ושב לאחוזתו:
notes.en: As it is stated: “According to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you”: that is, that it be in the buyer’s domain two years or more. And when he redeems it, he calculates the money that the buyer gave him for the field against the years from the time of sale until the Jubilee, and however much of the money comes to each year, so the buyer deducts for the seller according to the years it was in the buyer’s domain, as it is stated: “Then let him count the years of its sale,” that it was in the buyer’s domain, and according to them he deducts from the price of his redemption according to the reckoning of the price of the years, and the remainder of the money is returned to him, and he receives his field, as it is written: “And restore the surplus to the man to whom he sold it, and he shall return to his possession.”

messages.text: If one of those years was a year of blight or mildew, or if it was the Sabbatical Year, when the buyer is unable to derive benefit from the field, that year does not count as part of the tally, and the owner must wait an additional year before redeeming the field.

notes.he: השתי שנים דהא שני תבואות כתיב שתי שנים הראויין לתבואה תשהה ביד לוקח אבל היתה שנה הראויה לתבואה ונרה ולא זרעה או הובירה שהניחה בורה שאפי' ניר לא עשה בה איהו אפסיד אנפשיה ועולה לו במנין שתי השנים:
notes.en: Does not count toward the tally: of the two years, for it is written “years of crops”: two years fit for crops it must remain in the buyer’s hand. But if it was a year fit for crops and he plowed it and did not sow it, or left it fallow, that is, he left it uncultivated without even plowing it, he caused his own loss, and it counts for him toward the tally of the two years.

notes.dh: מתני' המוכר. היתה שנת שדפון וירקון או שביעית אינה עולה לו מן המנין
notes.he: בפ' המקבל (ב"מ דף קו.) מפרש שהשדפון וירקון הוה נמי כמו כן בכל העולם דאי השדפון בבאגא בהכי לא תנן דעולה לו מן המנין דיקא נמי דקתני דומיא דשביעית שאסור לזרוע בו (בכל העולם):
notes.en: Mishna. If it was a year of blight or mildew, or the Sabbatical Year, it does not count toward the tally: In the chapter HaMekabel (Bava Metzia 106a) it explains that the blight and mildew were likewise throughout the world, for if the blight was [only] in the valley, in such a case we did not learn [here whether] it counts for him toward the tally. This is also precise, since it teaches it alongside the Sabbatical Year, when it is forbidden to sow (throughout the world).

notes.he: היו אותן ב' שנים שהיתה ביד הלוקח שנת שדפון וירקון שלא גדלה התבואה או היתה שנה אחת מהן שביעית] אינה עולה לו מן המנין ממנין שני תבואות אלא צריך להניחה עוד ברשותו ב' שנים הראויות לזריעה ולתבוא' והא דאמרן דאינן עולה לו מן המנין הני מילי באונס בידי שמים כה"ג אבל אם פשע בה [שלא זרע] (שנרה ולא זרעה או הובירה שלא נרה ולא זרעה) עולה לו ממנין ב' שנים אע"ג דלא הוה בהו תבואות ורשאי המוכר לגאלה לאלתר לסוף ב' שנים:
notes.en: If those two years that it was in the buyer’s hand were a year of blight or mildew, when the grain did not grow, or if one of them was the Sabbatical Year,] it does not count for him toward the tally of the years of crops; rather, he must leave it further in his domain [until there are] two years fit for sowing and for crops. And what we said, that it does not count for him, applies only to an act of Heaven such as this; but if he was negligent with it [and did not sow] (that he plowed and did not sow, or left it fallow, that he did not plow and did not sow), it counts for him toward the tally of two years even though there were no crops in them, and the seller may redeem it immediately at the end of two years.

messages.text: If the buyer plowed the field but did not sow it, or if he left it fallow, that year counts as part of his tally, as it was fit to produce a crop.

notes.dh: נרה או הובירה עולה לו מן המנין
notes.he: בגמרא מפרש אמאי תנא נרה כיון דתנא הובירה דעולה כ"ש נרה והוה מצי למימר לא זו אף זו קתני:
notes.en: If he plowed it or left it fallow, it counts toward the tally: The Gemara explains why it teaches “plowed”: since it teaches that “left it fallow” counts, all the more so “plowed.” And one could say: it teaches “not only this, but even this.”

messages.text: If the owner of the field sold it to the buyer before Rosh HaShana and the field was full of produce, and the owner redeems the field after two years, that buyer consumes from the field’s produce three crops in two years. Although he received the field with its crop, he is not required to return it in the same state.

notes.he: אותה העומדת בה בשעת קנייה ושתי תבואות בשתי שנים שתהא בידו:
notes.en: Three crops: the one standing in it at the time of purchase, and two crops in the two years that it will be in his hand.

notes.he: פעמים שיאכל הלוקח שלש תבואות בב' שנים כיצד אם מכרה לו מלאה פירות לפני ר"ה הרי זה אוכל אותן פירות העומדות ולסוף שנה זו הנכנסת תבואה אחרת ולשנה השנית תבואה שלישית:
notes.en: [Rabbi Elazar says [the printed mishna reads Rabbi Eliezer]: Sometimes the buyer consumes three crops in two years. How so? If he sold it to him full of produce before Rosh HaShana, he consumes that standing produce, and at the end of this coming year another crop, and in the second year a third crop.

messages.caption: Two years of crops before the seller may redeem: which years count, and Rabbi Eliezer’s three crops in two years

messages.text: Gemara
The mishna does not teach that one cannot redeem his field before two years have elapsed; rather, the mishna teaches that one is not permitted to redeem it.
messages.quote: One who sells his field during a period when the Jubilee Year is in effect is not permitted to redeem it

notes.he: דליהוי משמע אינו דין שיכופו את הלוקח להחזיר לו בפדיון בפחות משתי שנים:
notes.en: Gemara. It does not teach “he does not redeem”: which would mean that it is not the law that the buyer is compelled to return it to him by redemption in less than two years.

messages.text: Evidently, the tanna of the mishna holds that there is also a prohibition involved in the matter, such that it is prohibited even to rattle dinars before the buyer in order to persuade him to sell back the field.

notes.he: למוכר להראות זוזין ללוקח כדי שייטב בעיניו להחזירה לו:
notes.en: That even rattling is also prohibited: for the seller to show coins to the buyer so that he will be pleased to return it to him.

notes.he: דאיסורא נמי איכא אם יגאלנה קודם השלמת ב' שנים דאפי'] קרקושי זוזי נמי אסיר כלומר שאסור לו למוכר אפי' להראות הזוזים השמורים לצורך הפדיון להראותם ללוקח בתוך אותם ב' שנים שזיכתה לו התורה שתהא ברשותו:
notes.en: Evidently: there is a prohibition too if he redeems it before the two years are complete, for] even rattling coins is prohibited; that is, the seller is forbidden even to show the coins set aside for the redemption, to show them to the buyer, during those two years that the Torah granted him, that it be in his domain.

messages.text: And it is not necessary to state this with regard to the seller, as he stands in violation of a positive mitzva, as it is written: “According to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you” (Leviticus 25:15), and the plural form “years” indicates a minimum of two years.

Rather, even the buyer stands in violation of a positive mitzva, as we require the fulfillment of another mitzva from the same verse: “According to the number of years after the Jubilee Year you shall buy from your neighbor,” and if the buyer returns the field before the two years elapse, the mitzva is not fulfilled.

notes.he: במספר שנים אחר היובל תקנה דמשמע שתהא קנויה לו שתי שנים ואי מהדר ליה מקמי הכי עובר בעשה:
notes.en: “Years you shall buy”: “According to the number of years after the Jubilee you shall buy,” which means that it should be bought by him for two years; and if he returns it to him before that, he transgresses a positive mitzva.

notes.he: אם יפייס לו שיגאלנה בתוך אותן ב' שנים:
notes.en: Even the buyer as well: if he persuades him to redeem it within those two years.

notes.he: אם יקבל הדמים:
notes.en: Stands in violation of a positive mitzva: if he accepts the money.

notes.he: ב' שנים שלימים וליכא:
notes.en: For we require “years you shall buy”: two full years, and there are not.

messages.text: The field is sold in principle, but it leaves the buyer’s possession immediately, and his money is not refunded.
messages.lead: § It was stated: With regard to one who sells his field during the Jubilee Year itself,

notes.he: ביובל וזה הלוקח איבד מעותיו:
notes.en: It is sold and goes out: at the Jubilee, and this buyer has lost his money.

notes.he: דלא הדרי זוזי:
notes.en: Rav said it is sold: that the money is not returned.

notes.he: שחוזרת לו ביובל:
notes.en: And goes out: that it returns to him at the Jubilee.

messages.text: It is not sold at all.

notes.he: והמעות חוזרין:
notes.en: It is not sold at all: and the money is returned.

notes.dh: שמואל אמר אינה מכורה כל עיקר
notes.he: דאפי' הדמים חוזרין לו:
notes.en: Shmuel said it is not sold at all: that even the money is returned to him.

messages.text: What is the reasoning of Shmuel? Shmuel derives his opinion via an a fortiori inference. And what, if a field that was already sold before the Jubilee Year leaves the possession of the buyer in the Jubilee Year, is it not logical that a field that was not yet sold is not sold at all during the Jubilee Year?
messages.quote: It is not sold at all

notes.he: קודם היובל:
notes.en: Already sold: before the Jubilee.

notes.he: שבשנת היובל אינה מכורה שחוזרת לבעלים אינו דין שלא תמכר כלל שהמעות חוזרין:
notes.en: That is not sold: that in the Jubilee Year it is not [considered] sold, since it returns to its owners; is it not logical that it is not sold at all, so that the money is returned?

messages.text: And according to Rav, do we not say that one may derive an a fortiori inference in this way? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:

notes.dh: [ולרב לית ליה ק"ו] ולרב לא אמרינן ק"ו כי האי גוונא והתניא יכול ימכור כו'
notes.he: ומה מכורה כבר כשהיא קטנה יוצאה בשעת נערות (נתרוקנה עצמה בסימניה) דקנה עצמה בסימנין:
notes.en: [And according to Rav, is there no a fortiori inference?] And according to Rav, do we not say an a fortiori inference in such a case? But isn’t it taught: One might have thought a person may sell, and so on. And what, if [a daughter] already sold when she is a minor goes out at the time of young womanhood (she is released by her signs), for she acquires herself with the signs,

messages.text: One might have thought that a person may sell his daughter as a maidservant when she is a young woman. You can say the following a fortiori inference to reject such a possibility: And what, if a daughter who was already sold, now leaves her master upon becoming a young woman, is it not logical that a daughter who was not sold is not capable of being sold once she becomes a young woman?

notes.he: אמה העברייה יוצאה בסימני נערות כדתניא (קדושין דף ד.) ויצאה חנם אלו ימי נערות:
notes.en: A Hebrew maidservant goes out with the signs of young womanhood, as it is taught (Kiddushin 4a): “Then she shall go out for nothing”: these are the days of young womanhood.

notes.he: בשעת נערות אינו דין שלא תמכר שהמעות חוזרין אלמא אמרינן ק"ו כי האי גוונא:
notes.en: That is not sold: at the time of young womanhood, is it not logical that she is not sold, so that the money is returned? Evidently we say an a fortiori inference in such a case.

messages.text: Evidently, one may derive this type of an a fortiori inference. Why, then, does Rav disagree with Shmuel?

The cases are not comparable. There, with regard to a maidservant, once she becomes a young woman she is not ever sold again. Here, the field that is returned to the seller in the Jubilee Year may later be sold again. Rav therefore maintains that one may not derive the aforementioned a fortiori inference.

notes.he: בתו שמכר בקטנותה ויצאה בת חורין בסימני נערות לא הדרא ומזדבנא לעולם כדאמרינן (קדושין דף יח.) ואין אדם מוכר בתו לשפחות אחר שפחות דנפקא לן מבבגדו בה כיון שבגד בה שמכרה לשפחות שוב אינו יכול למוכרה הלכך יציאה גמורה היא ואיכא למימר ק"ו דאי מזדבין לה בימי נערות דאינה מכורה אבל שדה היוצאה לבעלים ביובל הדרא ומזדבנא לאחר היובל אם ירצה הלכך בשנת היובל נמי רשאי למוכרה ויוצאה לו בחנם:
notes.en: There: his daughter whom he sold in her minority and who went out free with the signs of young womanhood is never sold again, as we say (Kiddushin 18a): A person may not sell his daughter as a maidservant after [she was already] a maidservant, which we derive from “seeing he has dealt deceitfully with her”: once he has dealt deceitfully with her by selling her as a maidservant, he can no longer sell her. Therefore it is a complete going out, and one can say the a fortiori inference, that if he sells her in the days of young womanhood she is not sold. But a field that goes out to its owners at the Jubilee is sold again after the Jubilee if he wishes; therefore in the Jubilee Year, too, he may sell it, and it goes out to him for free.

notes.he: פי' רש"י בתו שמכרה בקטנותה ויצאה בת חורין בסימני נערות לא הדרא ומזבנא כדאמר בקדושין (דף יח. ושם) דאין אדם מוכר בתו לשפחות אחר שפחות כדנפקא לן מבבגדו בה כיון שבגד בה שמכרה לשפחות שוב אינו יכול למוכרה הלכך יציאה גמורה היא ואיכא למימר ק"ו עכ"ל ול"נ דהא פלוגתא דתנאי היא התם לכך פירש ר"י דאפי' למ"ד בעלמא דאדם מוכר בתו לשפחות אחר שפחות היכא דהביאה סימנים מיהא [מודה דלא מזדבנא] איכא ק"ו (דלא מזדבנא) מיהו ק"ק גבי מוכר שדהו נמי אתיא מהאי ק"ו דלא תימכר עוד מיהו יש לחלק דלא דמיא לק"ו דבתו כיון שבאו לה סימני נערות לא יפרקו עוד מעליה אבל מוכר שדהו בשעת היובל אין הק"ו טוב כל כך כמו גבי מוכר בתו שהרי היובל יעבור ויהיה כבתחלה ועוד יש לפרש כמו שפרש"י לפי שאין אדם מוכר בתו לשפחות אחר שפחות ואע"ג דפליגי בה תנאי מיהו קיימא לן כר"ש דסבירא ליה התם דאסור למכור:
notes.en: There, she is not sold again: Rashi explained: His daughter whom he sold in her minority and who went out free with the signs of young womanhood is not sold again, as it says in Kiddushin (18a) that a person may not sell his daughter as a maidservant after [she was] a maidservant, as we derive from “seeing he has dealt deceitfully with her”: once he dealt deceitfully with her by selling her as a maidservant, he can no longer sell her; therefore it is a complete going out, and one can say the a fortiori inference. Thus far his words. But this does not seem right, for that is a dispute of tanna’im there. Therefore the Ri explained that even according to the one who says elsewhere that a person may sell his daughter as a maidservant after [she was] a maidservant, where she has at least brought signs [of young womanhood, he agrees that she is not sold]; so there is an a fortiori inference. However, it is somewhat difficult: with one who sells his field, too, it should follow from this a fortiori inference that it is not sold anymore. However, one can distinguish: it is not like the a fortiori inference of his daughter, since once the signs of young womanhood have come to her they will not leave her again; but with one who sells his field at the time of the Jubilee, the a fortiori inference is not as strong as with one who sells his daughter, for the Jubilee will pass and it will be as at the start. And one can also explain as Rashi explained, that a person may not sell his daughter as a maidservant after [she was] a maidservant; and although tanna’im disagree about it, we hold like Rabbi Shimon, who holds there that it is forbidden to sell [her again].

notes.he: בבתו נערה משום הכי אמרינן ק"ו שאינה נמכרת כלל:
notes.en: There: with his daughter who is a young woman; for that reason we say an a fortiori inference that she is not sold at all.

notes.he: כלל שוב לעולם מאחר שהיא נערה:
notes.en: For she is not sold again: ever again, once she is a young woman.

notes.he: במוכר שדהו בשנת היובל כיון דאחר היובל מצי למיהדר ומזדבנא מכירה גמורה משום הכי בשנת היובל [נמי] מכורה ויוצא ולא הדרי זוזי ולא אמרינן [הכא] ק"ו:
notes.en: Here: with one who sells his field in the Jubilee Year, since after the Jubilee it can be sold again in a complete sale, for that reason in the Jubilee Year [too] it is sold and goes out, and the money is not returned, and we do not say an a fortiori inference [here].

messages.text: The Gemara raises an objection to Rav’s opinion from a baraita:

The verse states: “According to the number of years after the Jubilee you shall buy from your neighbor” (Leviticus 25:15). The term: After the Jubilee, teaches that a field may be sold in the year adjacent to the Jubilee Year.

verse.he: בְּמִסְפַּר שָׁנִים אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל תִּקְנֶה מֵאֵת עֲמִיתֶךָ בְּמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי־תְבוּאֹת יִמְכׇּר־לָךְ׃
verse.en: In buying from your neighbor, you shall deduct only for the number of years since the jubilee; and in selling to you, you shall be charged only for the remaining crop years:

notes.he: משמע אחר היובל מיד:
notes.en: After the Jubilee: means immediately after the Jubilee.

notes.he: שאם תקנה שדה תהא בידך שתי שנים בעל כרחו של מוכר ואפילו הוא רוצה לפדותה:
notes.en: “Years you shall buy”: that if you buy a field, it shall be in your hand two years against the seller’s will, even if he wants to redeem it.

notes.he: היינו דכתיב במספר שנים אחר היובל תקנה:
notes.en: “After the Jubilee… years you shall buy”: that is what is written: “According to the number of years after the Jubilee you shall buy.”

notes.he: לאלתר מיד אחר [שעבר יובל] לשני תבואות לב' שנים:
notes.en: Teaches that one may sell: immediately, right after [the Jubilee has passed], for years of crops, for two years.

messages.text: From where is it derived that a field may be sold in a year that is separated from the Jubilee Year? The verse states: “According to the multitude of the years you shall increase the price thereof, and according to the fewness of the years you shall diminish the price of it” (Leviticus 25:16). The verse teaches that one may sell a field even after several years have elapsed since the last Jubilee Year.

verse.he: לְפִי ׀ רֹב הַשָּׁנִים תַּרְבֶּה מִקְנָתוֹ וּלְפִי מְעֹט הַשָּׁנִים תַּמְעִיט מִקְנָתוֹ כִּי מִסְפַּר תְּבוּאֹת הוּא מֹכֵר לָךְ׃
verse.en: the more such years, the higher the price you pay; the fewer such years, the lower the price; for what is being sold to you is a number of harvests.

notes.he: שיהיה עד היובל תרבה מקנתו תמכרנה ביוקר שהרי עד היובל תהא קנויה לו אם לא יפדנה ולפי מעוט השנים תמכרנה בזול כדי שלא תונה את חבירך. ושמעינן מהנך קראי דמוכרין בין בסמוך ליובל שעבר בין מופלג ממנו כמה שנים:
notes.en: According to the multitude of the years: that remain until the Jubilee, you shall increase its price: you shall sell it dearly, for it will be bought by him until the Jubilee if he does not redeem it. And according to the fewness of the years, you shall sell it cheaply, so that you do not wrong your fellow. And we learn from these verses that one may sell both close to the Jubilee that has passed and several years removed from it.

notes.he: שמוכרין נמי ברחוק מן היובל כמו עשר שנים [לאחר היובל] או עשרים שנים לאחר היובל:
notes.en: Separated from the Jubilee, from where: that one may also sell far from the Jubilee, such as ten years [after the Jubilee] or twenty years after the Jubilee.

notes.he: ת"ל לפי רוב השנים [ולפי מעוט השנים לפי] רוב השנים היינו שמכרה סמוך ליובל שיש לו עוד שנים רבות עד היובל:
notes.en: The verse states: “According to the multitude of the years [and according to the fewness of the years]”: “according to the multitude of the years” is where he sold it close to the [previous] Jubilee, so that he still has many years until the Jubilee.

notes.he: כלומר שמכרה מופלג מן היובל שלא נשארו אלא מעט שנים עד [שנת] היובל:
notes.en: And according to the fewness of the years: that is, he sold it far from the Jubilee, so that only a few years remain until the Jubilee [Year].

messages.text: And in the Jubilee Year itself one may not sell his field, and if one sold it, it is not sold.
This baraita clearly seems to contradict the opinion of Rav.

The baraita means that the field is not sold for the number of years of the crops, i.e., it does not remain in the buyer’s possession for a minimum of two years, rather it is sold in principle, and then immediately leaves the buyer’s possession.
messages.quote: and if one sold it, it is not sold

notes.he: שלא תשהה ביד הלוקח כלום שהרי באותה שנה עצמה לקחה מידו אבל מכורה היא לכך שיאבד מעותיו:
notes.en: For the number of years of crops: that it does not remain in the buyer’s hand at all, for in that very year [the owner] takes it from him; but it is sold to the extent that he loses his money.

notes.he: בשנת היובל לענין מספר שני תבואות שיהא יכול הלוקח לתופשה ב' שנים:
notes.en: [Rav could say to you: it is not sold: in the Jubilee Year, with regard to the number of years of crops, that the buyer could hold it for two years.

notes.he: אבל מכורה היא דלא הדרי זביני ויוצאה ביובל:
notes.en: But it is sold: in that the sale is not retracted, and it goes out at the Jubilee.

messages.text: But if the field is indeed sold, let it stand in the buyer’s possession until after the Jubilee Year, and after the Jubilee Year let him consume the field’s produce for two years of crops, and only then return the field.
messages.quote: rather it is sold in principle

notes.he: לאחר שתי שנים ליהדרה בחנם בשביל יובל שעבר עליה מי לא תניא וכו':
notes.en: And we ask: “But if it is indeed sold”: after two years let him return it for free, on account of the Jubilee that passed over it. Isn’t it taught, and so on.

notes.he: כדקאמרת דלא הדרי זוזי תיהוי ליה ללוקח הנהו זוזי דיהב זביני דתיקום ברשותיה עד בתר יובל ובתר יובל ניכלה שני תבואות וניהדרא בלא דמים כמו שהיתה יוצאה ביובל בלא דמים]:
notes.en: But if it is indeed sold: as you say, that the money is not returned, let those coins that the buyer gave be a purchase for him, that it stand in his domain until after the Jubilee; and after the Jubilee let him consume [it for] years of crops and return it without money, just as it would go out at the Jubilee without money.]

messages.text: If the buyer consumed the field’s produce for one year before the Jubilee Year, he completes another year after the Jubilee Year?

notes.he: [מכרה לו שנה אחת לפני יובל ואכלה שנת אחת לפני יובל משלימין לו שנה שניה אחרת לאחר יובל] אלמא דיובל לא פקע זביניה:
notes.en: Isn’t it taught: [If he sold it to him one year before the Jubilee and he consumed it one year before the Jubilee, one completes for him a second year, another one, after the Jubilee]; evidently the Jubilee does not cancel his sale.

messages.text: The cases are not comparable. There, the buyer already entered the field in order to consume the produce, and therefore he completes the minimum of two years. Here, the buyer did not enter the field to consume the produce at all, as ownership of the field immediately reverts to the seller.

notes.he: שהרי קודם היובל התחיל לאוכלה הלכך מקיימינא ליה קרא כדכתיב שני תבואות אבל הקונה בשנת היובל לא נחית לאכילה:
notes.en: He entered to consume it: for he began consuming it before the Jubilee; therefore we fulfill the verse for him, as it is written: “years of crops.” But one who buys in the Jubilee Year did not enter to consume it.

notes.he: כיון דאכלה שנה אחת כבר לפני יובל הלכך משלימין לו לאחר יובל:
notes.en: [There, he entered to consume: since he already consumed it one year before the Jubilee, therefore one completes it for him after the Jubilee.

notes.he: במכרה בשנת יובל דלא נחית לאכילה קודם יובל כלום הלכך לא מצי למיכלה בתר יובל מספר שני תבואות אלא מכורה ויוצאה:
notes.en: Here: where he sold it in the Jubilee Year, he did not enter to consume anything before the Jubilee; therefore he cannot consume the number of years of crops after the Jubilee, but it is sold and goes out.

messages.text: § I learned two halakhot from Master Shmuel. One was this halakha, that if one sells his field during the Jubilee Year the sale is ineffective.

notes.he: דאמר שמואל אינה מכורה כל עיקר:
notes.en: One was this: that Shmuel said it is not sold at all.

notes.he: שמואל אמר אינה מכורה:
notes.en: One was this: Shmuel said it is not sold.

messages.text: And the other halakha concerned one who sells his Canaanite slave to gentiles, or to a Jew who resides outside of Eretz Yisrael, that the slave is emancipated.

notes.he: דהמוכר עבדו לעובד כוכבים קונסין אותו לפדותו ויפטרנו לחירות משום דאפקעיה ממצות וכן המוכר עבדו אפי' לישראל בחוצה לארץ יצא לחירות:
notes.en: Goes out to freedom: for one who sells his slave to a gentile is penalized to redeem him and free him, because he removed him from mitzvot. And likewise one who sells his slave even to a Jew outside the Land: he goes out to freedom.

notes.he: המוכר עבדו לעובד כוכבים קונסין רבו שיפדנו ויוצא לחירות:
notes.en: One who sells his slave to a gentile: one penalizes his master to redeem him, and he goes out to freedom.

notes.he: או אם מכרו לישראל בחוצה לארץ קונסין ללוקח ויוצא לחירות:
notes.en: Or if he sold him to a Jew outside the Land: one penalizes the buyer, and he goes out to freedom.

messages.text: A Canaanite slave is partially obligated in the fulfillment of mitzvot. By selling him to a gentile, one prevents him from fulfilling the mitzvot, and by selling him to one who dwells outside of Eretz Yisrael, one prevents him from fulfilling the mitzva of dwelling in Eretz Yisrael. The Sages therefore decreed that the Jewish master must write the slave a bill of manumission after the sale, so that if he runs away from his gentile master, he would not reenter servitude under the Jewish master.

With regard to one of these halakhot, Shmuel said that the sale is retracted and the money is refunded, and with regard to one of them, he said that the sale is not retracted and the buyer loses his money. But I do not know in which of the cases the sale is retracted and in which case it is not.

notes.he: מחדא מהנך תרתי שמעית מיניה דמר שמואל שהמקח בטל והמעות חוזרין או מהך דהמוכר שדהו בשנת היובל עצמה או מהך דהמוכר עבדו לישראל בחוצה לארץ:
notes.en: In one, the sale is retracted: of these two, I heard from Master Shmuel that [in one] the sale is void and the money is returned: either in the case of one who sells his field in the Jubilee Year itself, or in the case of one who sells his slave to a Jew outside the Land.

notes.he: אלא הלוקח מפסיד המעות ולא ידענא בהי מינייהו המקח בטל. ואי קשיא פשיטא דמהך דהמוכר שדהו בשנת היובל קאמר שמואל דהמקח בטל והמעות חוזרין דאם מעות אבודין מאי איכא בין רב לשמואל איכא בינייהו אי שמיט לוקח וקצצן אילנות שהיו בה לרב דאמר מכורה היא שדה הדרא ואילנות דקץ קץ לשמואל דאמר אינה מכורה ומעות מתנה הדרי אילנות ואע"ג דלוקח לא שקל זוזי אי נמי כגון שמכר עמה מטלטלין והחזיק לוקח בקרקעות ולא משך המטלטלין דקיימא לן (קידושין כו.) נכסים שאין להם אחריות נקנין עם נכסים שיש להם אחריות בכסף בשטר ובחזקה ואין צריך משיכה לרב דאמר מכורה ויוצאה שדה הדרא ומטלטלין מיקנו לשמואל דאמר אינה מכורה ומעות מתנה לא מיקנו מטלטלי דחזקה דקרקע לא הויא חזקה:
notes.en: And in one, the sale is not retracted: rather, the buyer loses the money; and I do not know in which of them the sale is void. And if it is difficult: It is obvious that it is about one who sells his field in the Jubilee Year that Shmuel says the sale is void and the money is returned, for if the money is lost, what difference is there between Rav and Shmuel? There is a difference between them if the buyer went ahead and cut down trees that were in it. According to Rav, who said it is sold, the field returns, and the trees he cut, he has cut [and keeps]; according to Shmuel, who said it is not sold and the money is a gift, the trees are returned, even though the buyer does not take back money. Alternatively, such as where he sold movable property along with it, and the buyer took possession of the land [by an act of ḥazaka] and did not pull the movable property, for we hold (Kiddushin 26a): Property that does not serve as a guarantee is acquired along with property that serves as a guarantee by money, by a document or by ḥazaka, and does not require pulling. According to Rav, who said it is sold and goes out, the field returns and the movable property is acquired; according to Shmuel, who said it is not sold and the money is a gift, the movable property is not acquired, for the ḥazaka of the land is not a [valid] ḥazaka.

notes.dh: ולא ידענא הי מינייהו המקח בטל
notes.he: ואי קשיא פשיטא דאהך דהמוכר שדהו בשנת היובל קאמר שמואל דהמקח בטל ומעות חוזרים דאי מעות אבודין מאי [איכא] בין רב לשמואל איכא בינייהו אי שמיט לוקח וקצץ אילנות שהיו בה לרב דאמר מכורה [היא] שדה הדרא בעינא ואילנות דקץ קץ לשמואל דאמר אינה מכורה ומעות מתנה הדרי אילנות ואע"ג דלוקח לא שקיל זוזי אי נמי כגון שמכר עמה מטלטלין והחזיק הלוקח בקרקעות ולא משך המטלטלין דקיימא לן נכסים שאין להן אחריות נקנים עם נכסים שיש להן אחריות בכסף בשטר ובחזקה ואין צריך משיכה לרב דאמר מכורה [ויוצאה] שדה הדרא ומטלטלי מיקנו לשמואל דאמר אינה מכורה ומעות מתנה לא מיקנו מטלטלי דחזקה דקרקע לא הוי חזקה עכ"ל רש"י ולפי האי שפרש"י דאמר במכור חוזר לבעליו מיד מ"מ מיקנו מטלטלין בהדייהו מקשין העולם מההיא דפ"ק דב"מ (דף יא.) מעשה בר"ג וזקנים שהיו באים בספינה אמר מעשר שאני עתיד למוד נתון ליהושע ומקומו מושכר לו (ואיכא בתוספתא) [ותני בסיפא] דנתקבלו שכר זה מזה וליתבי ההוא אתרא במתנה ע"מ להחזיר (או) וליקני לו בחליפין דסודר אי נמי לישייליה ההוא אתרא ויקנה ליה בקנין סודר וי"ל דכל דבר החוזר לבעלים כגון מתנה ע"מ להחזיר א"נ שאלה או שכירות בכולם לא מיקנו בחליפין משום דהוה כמו טובת הנאה דאמרינן (שם:) דאינה ממונא לקנות בחליפין ומש"ה הוצרך שיתקבלו מעות זה מזה:
notes.en: In brief: And I do not know in which of them the sale is void: Tosafot first quotes Rashi in full: it would seem obvious that the field sold in the Jubilee Year is the case where the sale is void and the money returned, for otherwise what would differ between Rav and Shmuel? There is a difference: trees the buyer cut down, or movable property sold along with the land and acquired through the buyer’s ḥazaka of the land (Kiddushin 26a); according to Rav the trees and the movable property stay with the buyer, and according to Shmuel they do not. Tosafot then raises the question people ask on Rashi’s view that the field is sold though it returns to its owner at once, and movable property is still acquired along with it: in the incident of Rabban Gamliel and the Elders on a ship (Bava Metzia 11a), he gave the tithe he would measure out to Rabbi Yehoshua and rented him its place, and the end of the account teaches that they received payment from one another. Why not give the place as a gift on condition that it be returned, or have it acquired by exchange [ḥalifin] with a cloth, or lend the place and have it acquired by a cloth? Tosafot answers: anything that returns to its owner, such as a gift on condition that it be returned, a loan or a rental, is not acquired by ḥalifin, since it is like a benefit of discretion, which (Bava Metzia 11b) is not money that can be acquired by ḥalifin; that is why they needed to receive payment from one another. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: המעות ללוקח:
notes.en: In one the sale is retracted: the money [is returned] to the buyer.

messages.text: Let us see if it is possible to resolve Rav Anan’s dilemma. It may be resolved from that which is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: But I do not know in which of the cases the sale is retracted

messages.text: In the case of one who sells his slave to a Jew outside of Eretz Yisrael, the slave is emancipated but nevertheless requires a bill of manumission from his second master.

Conclude from the baraita as follows: Since the baraita calls the second owner the slave’s master, and requires him to emancipate the slave, evidently the sale is not retracted, and the buyer loses his money.

notes.he: והלוקח מפסיד וכיון דבההיא חזינן דלא הדרי זביני ודאי כי אמר שמואל בהא אינה מכורה ומעות חוזרין:
notes.en: Evidently the sale is not retracted: and the buyer loses. And since in that case we see that the sale is not retracted, certainly when Shmuel said in this case that it is not sold, [he meant that] the money is returned.

messages.text: And therefore, when Shmuel says here that the field is not sold during the Jubilee Year, he means that the sale does not take effect and the money is returned to the buyer.

notes.he: מדקתני יצא לחירות וצריך גט שחרור מרבו שני] ש"מ דקנייה רבו שני ולא הדרי זביני המעות ללוקח דאי הוה הדרי זביני לא הוה צריך גט מרבו שני אלא מרבו ראשון. [ורב ענן. דאמר ולא ידענא הי מינייהו הדרי זביני]:
notes.en: Since it teaches that he goes out to freedom and requires a bill of manumission from his second master,] conclude from it that his second master acquired him and the sale is not retracted [so as to return] the money to the buyer; for if the sale were retracted, he would not need a bill from his second master but from his first master. [And Rav Anan, who said: I do not know in which of them the sale is retracted.] [The last words begin the Gemara’s next question, on 30a.]

messages.text: Continued on 30a: Rav Anan had not learned this baraita, and Shmuel’s words alone do not settle it: perhaps the field is not sold and the money is considered a gift, as Shmuel holds of one who betroths his sister.
